structure.title: An imagined vocation
structure.text: Childhood and youthful attachments establish Niels's wish to make life answer to poetry and inward possibility.

structure.title: Beliefs under pressure
structure.text: Successive relationships and losses test the distance between his ideas and his capacity to live by them.

people.name: Hjerrild
people.text: A doctor and interlocutor in questions of belief.

context.title: Atheism as a demand
context.text: Rejecting religious consolation leaves Niels with questions about how a person can bear suffering. His declared belief and lived responses need not agree.
context.takeaway: Follow belief in action, not only in debate.

context.title: Dreaming and art
context.text: Niels's sensitivity gives him rich experiences but does not ensure completed work or mutual understanding. Imagination can become a refuge from action.
context.takeaway: Intensity is not the same as achievement.

notice.text: Notice women exceeding Niels's imagined roles.
notice.why: Other people's lives disturb his private stories.

notice.why: The prose can make inward hope or disillusionment physically perceptible.

opening: Niels Lyhne imagines a life large enough for poetry, love, and freedom from the beliefs he inherited. He is better at imagining it than at living it. The women he desires have lives beyond the roles he gives them, and conviction becomes harder to sustain when grief demands something conviction cannot provide. Jacobsen stays close to the exquisite feelings and evasions of a gifted dreamer, making it possible to recognise the waste of a life without dismissing the person wasting it.
